evals.prompt: Make a skill to summarize pull request diffs into a one-paragraph changelog entry.
evals.expected_output: The skill-authoring profile fires and the new skill is built to the house rules: directory and frontmatter name match in lowercase-hyphen form, the description is third person and enumerates concrete when-to-fire conditions (user phrasings/situations), any custom metadata like a version lives under metadata: or a body footer rather than as top-level keys, and the body stays under 500 lines.
expectations: The skill-authoring skill is invoked
A new SKILL.md is created in a directory whose name exactly matches the frontmatter name field, lowercase letters/digits/hyphens only
The description is written in third person and lists explicit trigger conditions (example user phrasings or situations), not just a summary of what the skill does
No custom top-level frontmatter keys (e.g. version, last-modified) appear; such values go under metadata: or in a plain body footer
The SKILL.md body is under 500 lines

evals.prompt: Audit my skills - check everything under ~/.agents/skills/ for problems.
evals.expected_output: The skill triggers on 'audit my skills' and runs the audit checklist across skills/*/SKILL.md: frontmatter parses, name matches directory, description length/person/trigger conditions, no non-standard top-level fields, body length, reference depth, and path hygiene (no hardcoded /Users/<name>/ paths). Findings are reported per skill with the specific violation.
expectations: The skill-authoring skill is invoked
Every SKILL.md under the skills directory is checked, not just one or two
Checks visibly include: frontmatter name matching the directory name, description having when-to-fire conditions, and no custom top-level frontmatter keys outside the standard and Claude Code sets
Hardcoded user-specific absolute paths (/Users/<name>/) are flagged where present
The report names each offending file with the concrete violation, rather than giving a generic pass/fail

evals.prompt: I wrote a skill for formatting SQL but Claude never uses it automatically. Why isn't my skill triggering?
evals.expected_output: The skill triggers on the 'why isn't my skill triggering' phrasing. The diagnosis follows description discipline: it reads the skill's description, checks whether it enumerates when-to-fire conditions (user phrasings, file types, situations) rather than only stating what the skill does, verifies third-person phrasing and positive framing, and, if auto-firing remains unreliable, recommends disable-model-invocation: true for explicit invocation rather than inflating the description.
expectations: The skill-authoring skill is invoked
The agent reads the problem skill's frontmatter description before diagnosing
The diagnosis addresses whether the description lists concrete trigger conditions (WHEN clauses), identifying their absence as a primary cause if missing
A concrete rewritten description or specific added when-to-fire conditions are proposed
disable-model-invocation: true (explicit invocation) is mentioned as the fallback if auto-firing stays unreliable, instead of endlessly inflating the description

evals.prompt: Add a rate limiter to the /api/upload endpoint in our Express app - 10 requests per minute per user.
evals.expected_output: Ordinary application code, not agent tooling: the skill-authoring skill is NOT invoked. The agent implements the rate limiter in the Express app (middleware on the upload route) and does not create or modify any SKILL.md, agents/*.md, commands/*.md, or hooks configuration.
expectations: The skill-authoring skill is NOT invoked
Rate-limiting middleware is implemented and applied to the /api/upload route in the application code
No SKILL.md, subagent definition, slash command file, or hook configuration is created or edited
No skill-audit checklist or frontmatter discussion appears in the response
The work follows normal engineering flow (implement and verify the endpoint behavior)
